source.incomeTax: https://www.estv2.admin.ch/stp/kb/sg-de.pdf (Kantonsblatt St. Gallen, Stand Februar 2026, citing Art. 50 StG); cross-checked against https://www.sg.ch/content/dam/sgch/steuern-finanzen/steuern/formulare-und-wegleitungen/einkommens-und-vermoegenssteuer/tarife-und-steuerfuesse/tarife-privatpersonen-gueltig-ab/Tarif_2026_SG_DEF.pdf
source.municipalData: https://www.sg.ch/steuern-finanzen/steuern/steuerkalkulator/steuerfuss-uebersicht-aller-sg-gemeinden.html (interactive canton tool, per-letter pages, scraped for Steuerjahr 2026); BFS municipality register for Gemeinde-Nr / Wahlkreis

notes:
YEAR: 2026 figures used throughout. St. Gallen's Art. 50 Abs. 1/2 StG bracket table for income tax was explicitly re-indexed 'ab Steuerperiode 2026' (kalte Progression adjustment; several thresholds carry an asterisk in the law text marking the 2026-specific values, distinct from the 2025 table). The cantonal multiplier (105%) and the municipal Steuerfuss table were both confirmed current for 2026 via the canton's live Steuerfuss lookup tool (scraped per-municipality, dated with an explicit 'im Jahr 2026' label per row) and the 2026 budget message ('Steuerfuss unverändert bei 105 Prozent'). MECHANISM: like ZH/AG, SG computes an 'einfache Steuer' from the bracket table below and then the canton applies its own multiplier (105%, appliedOnTop=true) plus each municipality applies its own separate multiplier (Politische Gemeinde, which in SG's own tables already nets together the political-municipality and, where applicable, Ortsgemeinde/other local components into one 'Gesamtsteuerfuss der Gemeinde' figure -- SG does NOT publish a separate school-tax multiplier the way Thurgau does), and each Kirchgemeinde (parish) applies its own multiplier for members of that faith. QUIRK 1 -- INCOME TAX BRACKETS ARE WIDTH-BASED, NOT CUMULATIVE-THRESHOLD: Art. 50 Abs. 1 StG states the schedule as literal marginal WIDTHS ('0% für die ersten Fr. 11'600; 4% für die weiteren Fr. 4'200; 6% für die weiteren Fr. 18'000; ...'), which was converted here directly into cumulative {from,rate} breakpoints by summing the widths (11600, +4200=15800, +18000=33800, +26500=60300, +38100=98400, +166100=264500). QUIRK 2 -- FLAT-RATE CAP ABOVE FR. 264'500 (Art. 50 Abs. 2 StG): 'Für steuerbare Einkommen über Fr. 264'500 beträgt die einfache Steuer für das ganze Einkommen 8,5 Prozent' -- i.e. above this threshold the LAW does not describe a marginal bracket at all; it redefines the ENTIRE tax as a flat 8.5% of the WHOLE income (not just the excess). This was verified to be numerically self-consistent with continuing the progressive schedule at a marginal rate of 8.5% (progressive-sum tax at Fr. 264'500 = Fr. 22'486.60 vs. flat-rate tax = Fr. 264'500 x 8.5% = Fr. 22'482.50 -- a ~Fr. 4 rounding-level difference caused by the law's round-Franken bracket widths, not a real discontinuity). Because the derivative of 'flat 8.5% of whole income' is still 8.5%, the table above correctly represents this as a final marginal breakpoint {from: 264500, rate: 0.085} and monotonicity holds throughout (verified programmatically). A developer should be aware the CANTON'S OWN legal formula is 'multiply the whole income by 8.5%' above the threshold, not 'apply 8.5% to the excess on top of the cumulative tax from lower brackets' -- the two are only equal up to sub-Fr.5 rounding noise, so either formula is acceptable in practice. SPLITTING (married filers): Art. 50 Abs. 3 StG: 'Für gemeinsam steuerpflichtige Ehegatten wird der Steuersatz des halben steuerbaren Einkommens angewendet' (Vollsplitting divisor 2.0 -- functionally identical to Thurgau's explicit divisor-2.0 language despite the different wording). This means tax_married(income) = 2 x tax_single(income / 2), which is mathematically equivalent to simply DOUBLING every single-schedule breakpoint threshold while keeping the same marginal rates (proof: d/d(income)[2 x tax_single(income/2)] = tax_single'(income/2), i.e. the marginal rate at doubled threshold 2T equals the marginal rate at T in the single schedule). The 'married' array above was derived this way (not a separately published table) and verified self-consistent/monotonic. The same reduced-rate mechanism (Abs. 4) also extends to widowed/separated/divorced/single taxpayers who live with children or dependants and support them, using the same halved-income rate lookup. WEALTH TAX: genuinely flat, not bracketed -- Art. 65 Abs. 1 StG: 'Die einfache Steuer vom steuerbaren Vermögen beträgt 1,7 Promille' (1.7 per-mille = 0.0017 decimal), represented as a single {from:0, rate:0.0017} entry. Social deductions from net wealth (Fr. 75'000 per taxpayer, plus Fr. 20'000 per minor child) apply before this flat rate but are deduction amounts, not rate brackets, and are not encoded in this bracket table (this project's convention per the deduction-simplification scope decision). CHURCH TAX: does NOT have a single canton-wide reformed/catholic rate -- both reformed ('evangelisch') and Roman Catholic ('katholisch') multipliers are set independently by each of SG's ~90 Kirchgemeinden (parish boundaries do not always align 1:1 with the 75 political municipalities: several municipalities are split across multiple Kirchgemeinden, e.g. St. Gallen itself has three separate Kirchgemeinde subdivisions -- Centrum/Tablat/Straubenzell -- and Oberriet is split into Kriessern/Montlingen/Kobelwald with different Catholic rates). SG_municipalities.json therefore uses the DEFAULT/primary parish figure per municipality as scraped from the canton's live per-municipality lookup tool; sub-parish variation is not separately encoded (see the source PDF in data/raw/sources/SG_Steuerfuesse_Gemeinden_2025.pdf and the per-letter scraped pages for the full breakdown). One canton-wide FLAT rate does exist: the Christ-katholische Kirchgemeinde (Old Catholic church, a small minority denomination) is uniformly 24% across the entire canton -- stated explicitly in both the 2025 PDF ('Der Steuerfuss für Angehörige der christkatholischen Kirchgemeinde beträgt im ganzen Kanton 24 Prozent') and confirmed unchanged for 2026 in every scraped municipality row; this is NOT encoded as a separate JSON field since the app schema only has reformed/catholic slots, but is worth knowing if a Christ-katholisch option is ever added. DATA GAP -- WIL (SG), BFS 3427: the city of Wil's 2026 municipal multiplier is genuinely UNDECIDED as of the report date (2026-09-08) -- a binding referendum on the 2026 Steuerfuss is scheduled for 2026-09-27, with three competing proposals on the ballot (115%, 118%, or 121%; the city council recommends 121%, the city parliament 118%). The canton's own live lookup tool shows '0' for Wil's 2026 figures (church multipliers included, since those may also depend on the outcome), which was correctly preserved as null (municipalMultiplier and both church multipliers) in SG_municipalities.json rather than guessing a value -- this must be revisited once the vote result is published.

ERRATA (added 2026-09-11, after the app went live showing Wil with no municipal/church tax lines at all): per user request, the null values were replaced with reasonable estimates so Wil no longer looks like it has zero municipal tax, with the app UI updated to flag the estimate prominently rather than present it as a confirmed rate. municipalMultiplier is now 118 (the arithmetic mean of the three ballot proposals: 115, 118, 121 -- not a prediction of the outcome, just a defensible midpoint), municipalMultiplierEstimated=true. churchMultiplierReformed/Catholic are now 26/24 (the Wil-district average across the other 9 municipalities in the Wil Wahlkreis: Degersheim, Flawil, Jonschwil, Oberuzwil, Uzwil, Niederbüren, Niederhelfenschwil, Oberbüren, Zuzwil -- reformed ranged 23-28 averaging 25.7 rounded to 26, catholic ranged 21-27 averaging 24.1 rounded to 24), churchMultiplierEstimated=true. This MUST be revisited and replaced with the real confirmed rate once the 2026-09-27 referendum result is published -- do not treat these as a substitute for checking back. MUNICIPALITY COUNT: SG currently has 75 political municipalities (down from the ~77 once referenced historically -- Hemberg and Oberhelfenschwil merged into the new municipality Neckertal effective 2023; both legacy names still appear as zeroed-out historical rows on the canton's lookup tool and were excluded here), grouped into 8 Wahlkreise (which replaced the old Bezirke in 2003), matching the BFS municipality register used for bfsNumber/district joins exactly (75/75 matched with no manual overrides beyond stripping cantonal disambiguator suffixes like ' (SG)').
